item.title: M. Kat Anderson at The Avid Reader — Thu Sep 3, 11:30 AM — Avid Reader
item.description: Join The Avid Reader for an evening with author M. Kat Anderson as she discusses her latest book, I Sing to the Earth and She Sings Back. 📅 Thursday, September 3, 2026⏰ 6:30–7:30 PM📍 The Avid Reader | 617 2nd Street, Davis In I Sing to the Earth and She Sings Back, Anderson explores how we can deepen our relationship with the natural world and reconnect with earth-based wisdom. Through personal stories, ecological insight, and lessons gathered over decades of working alongside California Indigenous elders, she invites readers to slow down, rediscover wonder, practice reciprocity, attune to natural cycles, and see the living world in new ways. About the Author M. Kat Anderson is an ethnoecologist, writer, gardener, and gatherer whose work focuses on restoring relationships between people and native ecosystems. item.title: Thursday Live at the Odd Fellows: The Evie Ladin Band — Thu Sep 3, 12:00 PM — Davis Odd Fellows
item.description: Head to the Davis Odd Fellows Lodge for another Thursday Live, featuring the Evie Ladin Band and their captivating blend of old-time Americana, roots music, rhythm, and dance. 📅 Thursday, September 3, 2026🚪 Doors Open: 7:00 PM | Show: 7:30 PM📍 Davis Odd Fellows Lodge | 415 2nd Street, Davis🎟️ Donation Only The Evie Ladin Band brings together Evie Ladin, Keith Terry, and Erik Pearson for a lively performance rooted in Appalachian old-time music and influenced by African-diaspora traditions and contemporary life. Expect clawhammer banjo, resonant vocals, storytelling, inventive string music, and rhythmic dance in a show that blurs the line between music and movement. The band’s performances have been heard everywhere from A Prairie Home Companion to Hardly Strictly Bluegrass. Admission is donation only, with all donations going directly to support the musicians. item.title: Inside the Artist’s Studio Opening Reception — Fri Sep 4, 5:30 PM — Gallery 625
item.description: Join us at Gallery 625 for the opening reception of Inside the Artist’s Studio 2026! All are welcome to attend this free event that coincides with the downtown Woodland First Friday event. This exhibition celebrates the creative spaces of Yolo County Resident Artists. This non-juried exhibition is open to the first 30 Artists who deliver their artwork to Gallery 625, and each participating Artist will have an artwork and a photo of themselves in their studio on display. It’s a surprise which Artists will be included, so join us at the opening reception to find out which artworks are on display! The opening reception will be held on Friday, September 4, from 5:30 to 8:00 p.m. Light refreshments, Yolo County wine, and live music by Jon Spivack will round out the evening. Inside the Artist’s Studio will be on view at Gallery 625 from September 4 through October 30, 2026. item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Sep 5, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Tai Chi Basics — Sat Sep 5, 8:00 AM — Great Bear Vineyards
item.description: 🌿 Tai Chi Basics Course 🌿 Saturday, September 5 | 8–9am Start your Saturday with movement, mindfulness, and a little vineyard tranquility! ☀️🍇 Join us every Saturday morning for our Tai Chi Basics Course, a beginner-friendly introduction to this beautiful, slow-moving martial art. Tai Chi combines mindful movement, balance, strength, and fluidity to help you feel more grounded and connected. 🧘‍♀️✨ This introductory class focuses on foundational drills and postures designed to build balance, leg strength, coordination, and body awareness while preparing you for a deeper Tai Chi practice. 🌱 Leading the class is Daniel Pfister, who has practiced Tai Chi for nearly 30 years! item.title: Davis Farmers Market – Wednesday Evenings (50th Anniversary Year) — Wed Sep 9, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
The Davis Farmers Market continues every Wednesday in Central Park with new fall hours! Beginning Wednesday, September 2, the Wednesday market will be open from 3:00–6:00 PM, replacing the extended 4:00–8:00 PM Picnic in the Park hours. Stop by to shop for fresh, locally grown produce, artisan goods, prepared foods and other market favorites from local farmers and vendors. It’s a great opportunity to stock up for the week, meet up with friends, support local growers and food makers, and enjoy a beautiful afternoon in Central Park. The Davis Farmers Market is celebrating its 50th Anniversary in 2026, marking five decades of bringing fresh food, local farmers and the Davis community together. Wednesday Market Details:
Wednesdays from 3:00–6:00 PM Central Park in Downtown Davis Fresh, seasonal produce Artisan goods and prepared foods Local farmers and food makers Family-friendly and open to everyone
Free to attend – shop local and enjoy your Wednesday afternoon at the Davis Farmers

item.title: Gentle yoga — Tue Sep 22, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community This is a slow and mindful practice that emphasizes deep breathing, body awareness, and nervous system regulation. This class is accessible to all abilities, providing a supportive and trauma-informed space to reconnect with the body.
Sessions alternate between floor yoga and chair yoga (on the 2nd and 4th Tuesday). Stay a bit longer on the last Tuesday of the month and join us for coffee or tea afterward!
Like all our events, this class is free, donations are welcome.

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Nov 18, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants

item.title: Author Event: M. Kat Anderson — Thu Sep 3, 6:30 PM — The Avid Reader
item.description: M. Kat Anderson @ The Avid Reader Thursday Sep 3rd, 2026 | 6:30 PM – 7:30 PM About the Book – I Sing to the Earth and She Sings Back I Sing to the Earth and She Sings Back provides readers with practical, grounded tools for reclaiming earth-based wisdom. Each chapter explores a distinct pathway to intimacy with nature: slowing down to reimagine time; reawakening childlike wonder; seeing the sentience of other life forms; practicing reciprocity and partnership; attuning to seasonal and lunar cycles; and more. Throughout, M. Kat Anderson shares deep personal stories of her own quest to heal a sense of disconnection from the earth. As a non-Native author who has collaborated with California Indigenous elders for decades, she offers a perspective shaped by humility, curiosity, and a commitment to respectful engagement. In a voice both scholarly and soulful, she opens a door for non-Native readers seeking authentic belonging to nature without cultural appropriation. About the Author M.

item.title: Thursday Live! The Evie Ladin Band — Thu Sep 3, 7:30 PM — Davis Odd Fellows
item.description:
Thursday Live at the Odd Fellows At the Davis Odd Fellows Lodge September 3, 2026 The Evie Ladin Band Our shows are donation only. Your generous donations all go to the musicians. As always, our bar will be open to purchase beer, wine or sodas. Tenacious, innovative string musicians, the Evie Ladin Band – Evie Ladin, Keith Terry and Erik Pearson – throws down captivating, truly entertaining live shows. Grounded in Appalachian old-time repertoire, seasoned in African-diaspora roots, writing from life in modern cities, blurring the lines between music and dance, the polyrhythmic heat of Evie’s clawhammer banjo, resonant voice, real stories and rhythmic dance have been heard from A Prairie Home Companion to Hardly Strictly Bluegrass. Their performance experience is a stand-out. Doors open at 7p, show at 7:30p.
Source: The Dirt

item.description:

The result is Lucy’s collection of reimagined vintage Japanese textiles and Louise’s fine art gourds. Lucy focus is on history and repurposing, and Louise emphasizes nature and transformation. This show celebrates craftsmanship, East Asian influence, tradition, and human connection.

We will activate spaces across the UC Davis campus, in the City of Davis, and at community-hosted site visits. Explore cultural and artisan booths throughout I-House, enjoy food trucks out front, and experience a full lineup of performances on our backyard stage. It’s an open house in the truest sense: for the day, this is your house too, and every culture and community has a place here. I-Fest is a celebration, but your participation also supports the work I-House does all year long: welcoming newcomers, supporting English learners, and helping people from around the world find connection and community in Davis. At a time when many of us are feeling anxious or disconnected, creating spaces for joy, belonging, and connection feels more important than ever.
